title: General table: every process, and where each of the two penalties falls

the_dichotomy: The two penalties live in DIFFERENT FUSION KINDS and are almost disjoint. Width: 91% of its excess (61% + 30%) sits in two kLoop groups, the ones XLA emits 'one element of the root at a time' and therefore vectorises. Sawtooth: 79% of its gap sits in the Triton-emitted kCustom fusion, whose grid is the tile count and which XLA's width decision never touches. The rolls and the reductions are immune to width (+-1%).

triton_tile_model.finding: grid = PRODUCT over dims of ceil(dim / tile), with the tile taken from the fusion's backend_config block_level_fusion_config.output_tiles
triton_tile_model.note: num_warps=4 is the 128-thread block seen in every box
triton_tile_model.what_it_explains: The grid, exactly, in all four cases. And almost all of the lighter kernel's cost change (predicted -4.1 points, measured -4.5%).
triton_tile_model.what_it_does_NOT_explain: The heavy kernel keeps the SAME tile [4,1,8,16,3] at both B, so its blocks-per-replica rises only 3.1% (19.615 -> 19.000), yet its time per replica falls 26.8%. A residual of about 23% is unexplained.
triton_tile_model.tile_is_not_predictable: The tile along B is not fixed: Triton chose 4 and 8 at B=65, 4 and 16 at B=75, 8 and 8 at B=135, 4 and 16 at B=140. It is selected by Triton's own cost model per shape and moves non-monotonically, so the padding waste cannot be derived from B alone.
triton_tile_model.block_count_does_not_predict_cost: For the 65/75 pair the heavy kernel keeps the same tile, its blocks per replica rise only 3.1% (19.615 -> 19.000) and its time falls 26.8%. For the 135/140 pair the Triton group's blocks per replica FALL 14.9% (31.48 -> 26.79) while its cost RISES 27%. So the tile acts on efficiency, not on launch count.

the_opposition.status: RETRACTED as a general rule, kept for the reasoning trail
the_opposition.what_I_proposed: That width penalises B divisible by 4 while Triton tile padding penalises B not divisible by 4, giving a clean B mod 4 ranking.
the_opposition.why_it_is_wrong: It assumed the tile along B is always 4. The measurement shows it is 4, 8 or 16 depending on the shape, so the padding waste is not a function of B mod 4. At B=140 (a multiple of 4) one Triton kernel still wastes 2.86%, because its tile along B is 16.
the_opposition.what_survives: The width half is unaffected and still holds: width = min(4, 2^(v2(B)+v2(L))), verified on 89/89 grids and five devices. Only the tile half of the proposed ranking is withdrawn.
the_opposition.what_replaces_it: The sawtooth's proximate cause is Triton RE-TILING per batch size. Since the tile comes from Triton's cost model and moves non-monotonically, the sawtooth is not analytically predictable from B, which is exactly why interpolating the f(B) curve failed and why the survey had to measure it.

limits: The two experiments group kernels slightly differently: the width pair put loop_select_fusion_1 with the acceptance group, while fusion_doc puts it in the remainder. Compare rows by fusion kind and kernel name, not by group label alone.
The width axis is a single pair (135 vs 140) and the sawtooth axis a single pair (65 vs 75), one run each, at 3600 sweeps.
At the real production schedule the 65/75 gap is 0.6%, not 5.2%, so part of the sawtooth residual may be a short-schedule artefact rather than steady state.
This build exposes 79 XLA flags and NONE disables Triton fusion or the vectorisation width, so neither penalty has a flag-level lever here.

known: The grid of every Triton kernel equals the product of ceil(dim/tile) over its output_tiles, exact in 8 of 8 cases.
The emitter is Triton: backend_config carries kind="__triton" with an explicit block_level_fusion_config. num_warps=4 is the 128-thread block seen in every box.
Width lives in kLoop fusions (91% of its excess); the sawtooth lives in the Triton kCustom fusion (79% of its gap). Nearly disjoint.
Triton re-tiles per batch size, non-monotonically.
open: Why the SAME Triton kernel with the SAME tile runs about 23% less efficiently per block at B=65 than at B=75.
What drives Triton's tile choice, and whether it can be pinned.
Hardware counters were never read: no ncu in the Modal container, and the local RTX 5070 (sm_120) cannot use the Ubuntu-repo Nsight Compute 2024.1, which predates Blackwell support.
